page: Amazon Web Services c8i-flex.xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical Intel Xeon 6975P-C cores running at 3.9 GHz. The system is equipped with 8.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, yielding 2.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPUs, and it operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark results highlight strong single-core performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2110.0 and a single-threaded gzip compression rate of 34.08 GB/sec. However, multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics show some limitations. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance of 4301.36 and the PassMark memory score of 1660.88 fall into the lower performance tier. Large-block memory read and write operations maintain average throughput at 40.9 GB/sec and 28.5 GB/sec, respectively.

The c8i-flex.xlarge provides a cost-efficient entry point for compute-focused workloads that do not require massive memory footprints or local NVMe storage. Advanced vector and matrix extensions, including AVX-512 and AMX, are fully supported, making it capable of handling lightweight machine learning inference, such as prompt processing for small and medium LLMs. This server is well-suited for single-threaded processing tasks, software compilation, static web serving, and lightweight database operations.
